title: Apply a feedback report to the source skill
prompt: Harbor's feedback on our component skill came in: `tooling/react-skills/feedback/build-composable-components/2026-10-02-action-pending-state.md`. Our editable skill source is in `tooling/react-skills/`. Apply what's worth applying and tell me what you did with each point.

criteria.text: `tooling/react-skills/skills/build-composable-components/examples/action-menu.tsx` no longer has a root-level `loading` (or renamed equivalent such as `pending`/`busy`) that is ORed into every item's disabled state; the family has no family-wide loading context, and the feature adapter passes each item its own mutation's pending state (e.g. `disabled={duplicate.isPending}`). The rest of the example (trigger, content size/group selectors, className merge order, composition) is preserved, and the project typechecks.

The new guidance (pending/disabled state belongs to the action that runs it, not to the family) is stated once, in one destination (a numbered rule in SKILL.md or a focused reference linked from it), labeled with its layer, and is not repeated in SKILL.md rules plus checklist plus reference plus README. A rule that keeps the report's boundary (a consumer-set root `disabled` for a read-only record is still allowed) gets full credit; one that bans every root-level disabled or loading prop gets 0.5.

F-002 (className merged last) is recognized as already covered by existing SKILL.md rule 2: no second className rule or duplicate checklist line is added, and the handoff records it as already-covered, citing the existing rule.

F-003 is not implemented as a name-based check that fails on any prop called `loading` (the report itself says a single-action `loading` is legitimate); the handoff marks it rejected or adapted with that reason (the defect is semantic, a name match would encode formatting and produce false positives). Adding such a script is a fail.

SKILL.md still has `## Version`, `## Layer placement`, and `## Companion skill routing`, stays under 220 lines, and its frontmatter is intact. If any file was added, renamed, or removed in the skill folder, `registry.json` `files` matches the folder; README.md is updated only if the description of what the skill teaches changed. No adapters or unrelated files were hand-created.

The final message (REPORT.md) gives one decision per finding (F-001 accepted, F-002 already-covered, F-003 rejected/adapted, or equivalent wording) with destination, short reason, and the validation run (typecheck result). Unsupported claims are not presented as verified.
The feedback report file still exists with its findings and evidence intact (updating `status` to `applied` or adding a short decision note is fine; deleting or rewriting findings is a fail).

No edits under `src/`, no new dependencies, no changes to `tsconfig.json`, and no unrelated rewrites of other rules, the styling reference, or CHANGELOG entries for past versions. A new CHANGELOG entry for the change is fine but not required.
